title: God's Covenant with David
lead: God's promise, given through Nathan, that David's house, kingdom and throne would last forever. Later prophets and psalms built the hope for a coming king on it, and the New Testament reads it as fulfilled in Jesus.

sections.b: In 2 Samuel 7 God turns down David's plan to build him a house and promises instead to make David a house: an offspring whose kingdom God will establish, who will build a house for God's name, and to whom God will be a father. God's loyal love will not be taken from him as it was from Saul (2 Samuel 7:12–16; 1 Chronicles 17:11–14). The word "covenant" is not used in chapter 7, but later texts call it one (2 Samuel 23:5; Psalm 89:3–4; Psalm 132:11–12; Jeremiah 33:20–21). Psalm 89 holds God to the promise when the dynasty seems to fall. Prophets look for a shoot from Jesse's stump and a righteous Branch for David (Isaiah 11:1; Jeremiah 23:5; Ezekiel 34:23–24; Amos 9:11). A Dead Sea scroll, the Florilegium (4Q174), reads the promise of a son as the Branch of David of the last days. The New Testament applies it to Jesus (Luke 1:32–33; Acts 2:30; Acts 13:22–23; Romans 1:3; Hebrews 1:5).
